terms.comment: A description of ours, made like Traupman’s laterum strūctor, bricklayer: strūctor is the builder or mason (Cicero), tēgula the roof tile. The one ancient trade name we found, scandulārius, a layer of wooden shingles, is a single entry in the Digest (Lewis & Short), and is not a roofer of tiles.

phrases.latin: Tēgulārum strūctor in tēctō est; tēgulās frāctās mūtat.
phrases.english: The roofer is up on the roof, changing the broken tiles.

sources: Lewis & Short: structor · Lewis & Short: tegula · Lewis & Short: scandularius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 165, 283.
